principles.text: Build a clippable aha moment into the product: the user does something and the app shows a shareable result.
Find proven viral formats before scaling; the research is what makes the scale work.
Make the content the hook and the product the payoff; if the app is the entire video, nobody watches.
Cap payouts per post so every view past the cap is free reach and effective CPM keeps falling.
Volume beats polish: hundreds of imperfect clips from many accounts beat one perfect ad.

sampleQA.question: How should I set up a clipping campaign for my app?

answer.text: Find what works first. In one case study the app spent a month researching formats before scaling.
Write the creator brief like a course on making content for your app, not a requirements list.
Run several campaigns in parallel with different rates, caps and formats so you learn in weeks, not months.
Set a sensible payout cap per post; views past the cap are free reach.

sampleQA.question: Should I move budget from Meta ads to creator content?

answer.text: He argues people no longer trust branded content but treat regular people's posts like peer recommendations.
His comparison: pay regular people about $0.30 CPM for organic-looking posts instead of paying Meta to show ads people skip.
Stress-test the math: in his Netflix analysis, even at 10x too optimistic conversion, CAC is $12 instead of $89.

sampleQA.question: What makes a short-form clip perform?

answer.text: The hook decides most of the performance; he writes 5 hooks per campaign before opening the editor.
Retention matters: across 14,000 clips, those where 70%+ of viewers passed second 6 averaged 120k views.
Keep it simple; low-effort content looks less like an ad and blends into the feed.
Lead with something interesting and mention the product at the end.
